I will keep most of my land in the wheat-maize rotation, because that is the steadiest way for me to use my 10.1 mu, my well water, and the labor my family can still put in while some people work off-farm. I will put 8.0 mu into winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land, and I will keep 2.1 mu for cotton. I have farmed a long time, so I do not want to take risks with weak seed or very low input. On wheat and maize, I will use better seed and keep fertilizer at a moderate-to-strong level because irrigated land in my area can carry it and these two crops are the backbone of my income and grain supply. For cotton, I will keep a smaller area because it needs more management and spraying, but I will still plant it because it spreads risk and gives me some cash income. I will rely on rotary tillage for the wheat and cotton fields because it is practical for me, and I will use no-tillage for summer maize after wheat to save time and labor. With irrigation available, I will protect yield in key stages rather than farming too loosely.
